Package com.lucaf.robotic_core.KERN.K700

Class K700

java.lang.Object
com.lucaf.robotic_core.impl.SensorInterface
com.lucaf.robotic_core.impl.ScaleInterface
com.lucaf.robotic_core.KERN.K700.K700
public class K700 extends ScaleInterface
KERN 770/GS/GJ series weighing scale (internally code-named "K700"), adapted to the ScaleInterface abstraction.

Unlike the KERN PCB, which accepts bare single-letter commands, the 770 series expects every control command to be an ESC-prefixed sequence terminated by CR LF: 

   ESC P CR LF   — print/output the current result (used as the read command)
   ESC T CR LF   — tare
where ESC is ASCII 27. The scale's serial port must be configured for 7-bit ASCII characters with a parity bit (factory default: odd parity, 1 stop bit, 1200 baud) — this is set on the SerialParams the connection is opened with, not by this class.

Response format

Every answer is a fixed-width, 14 character frame (terminator excluded), followed by CR LF: 
   S B N1 N2 N3 N4 N5 N6 N7 N8 B U1 U2 U3
  • S — a space or a minus sign for negative weights
  • B — a space (separator)
  • N1..N8 — the weight, right aligned and padded with spaces, decimal point included
  • B — a space (separator)
  • U1..U3 — the unit ("g", "kg", ...), space padded
As with the PCB, the unit field is blanked out while the weight is still settling, which is what marks a reading as unstable rather than stable.

Instead of a plain "Error" payload, the 770 series reports faults as a special frame embedded in the same 14-character layout, e.g. " ERR X YZ " (system error) or a status letter pair such as "H*" (overload) / "L*" (underload) / "C*" (adjusting in progress) at the position the weight digits would otherwise occupy. Any frame that doesn't carry a valid decimal weight is treated as an error/unusable reading.

Framing

As with the PCB, the scale does not necessarily deliver a full frame in a single serial event, so incoming bytes are fed to a LineAssembler and only decoded once the CR LF terminator has been seen.

  • Method Details

    • read

      public ScaleResponse read() throws IOException
      Actively reads the current weight (stable or unstable) by sending ESC P CR LF and waiting for the response.

      The 770 series has no dedicated "stable only" command like the PCB's "s", so ScaleInterface.readStable() is not overridden and falls back to the base class's default of simply calling this method.

      Specified by:
      read in class ScaleInterface
      Returns:
      the current weight, or an error response if the scale did not answer
      Throws:
      IOException - if the read command cannot be sent or the wait is interrupted

    • enableEventReading

      public void enableEventReading()
      Enables the continuous reading stream. Incoming weights will be forwarded to consumers.

      Note: the 770 series only pushes data on its own if it has been put into "Auto print" mode via its own operating menu (codes 6-1-4 / 6-1-5). This class does not poll on a timer — it only forwards whatever the scale sends, whether that's in response to read() or, if the scale is in Auto print mode, unsolicited frames pushed continuously.

      Specified by:
      enableEventReading in class ScaleInterface
